structure.title: Page 001 - Agreement, Parties and Effective Date
structure.summary: A synthetic colocation and managed facilities agreement between Cedar Peak Infrastructure LLC (Provider) and Glasshaven Analytics Inc. (Customer), effective 15 February 2027, for Building DC-2 at Cedar Peak Data Campus in Briarfield, Colorado. Covers parties and purpose; contract documents and precedence (signed change orders, order form, agreement, schedules; marketing descriptions don't vary commitments); designated operational and contractual contacts. Grants a license (not a lease) to Suite D-14 with twelve 42U racks, 96 kW committed dual A/B power, up to four cross-connects, and access boundaries retained by Provider. Initial 36-month term from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030, with a five-Business-Day acceptance testing window and deemed acceptance. Optional 24-month renewal with 120 days' notice at list price less 8 percent. Fees: USD 18,600 monthly license charge, electricity billed at USD 0.14/kWh, cross-connects USD 175 monthly each. Security provisions are indicated but not detailed in this excerpt.

structure.title: Page 004 - Fees, Billing and Security
structure.summary: A synthetic colocation and managed facilities agreement between Cedar Peak Infrastructure LLC (Provider) and Glasshaven Analytics Inc. (Customer), effective 15 February 2027, covering Building DC-2 at the Cedar Peak Data Campus. It covers parties and contract documents, designated contacts, licensed space (Suite D-14, twelve racks, 96 kW power with A/B feeds, cross-connects, access boundaries), a 36-month term from 1 April 2027 with acceptance testing and a 24-month renewal at an 8% discount, fees (USD 18,600 monthly license, metered power at USD 0.14/kWh, cross-connects, USD 37,200 deposit, net 30 payment, 3% annual increases), service levels (99.95% power availability, incident severity response times, outage credits capped at 20%), physical security (CCTV, visitor and technician controls, breach notification within four hours), maintenance windows, remote hands billing, change control, and data responsibility and confidentiality, with Customer retaining data ownership and Provider not providing backup.

structure.title: Page 005 - Service Levels and Outage Credits
structure.summary: The text covers colocation service terms: invoicing monthly with net 30 payment and a refundable USD 37,200 security deposit usable for undisputed overdue charges after notice and a ten-day cure period; an annual 3% license increase starting 1 April 2028 and power rate changes requiring 60 days' notice and documented energy cost changes. Service levels include 99.95% monthly power availability at the rack PDU point, incident severity tiers with acknowledgement times (15 minutes for total A/B feed loss, 60 minutes for single-feed degradation), and credits of 2% of the monthly license charge per full 30 minutes of qualifying downtime, capped at 20%, with claims due within 20 days. Physical security requires continuous CCTV, badge logs, a staffed desk, 90-day footage retention, up to eight authorized technicians, 24-hour visitor registration with escorts, and breach notice within four hours. Maintenance occurs Sundays 02:00-06:00 Mountain Time with seven days' notice, with emergency exceptions. Remote hands include eight free hours monthly, then USD 110/hour. Customer change requests need 48 hours' method statements and may be rejected if risky. Customer retains data ownership and control; provider does not inspect content or provide application backup.

structure.title: Page 006 - Physical Security and Visitor Controls
structure.summary: Covers payment and deposit terms: monthly invoices payable net 30, a refundable USD 37,200 security deposit usable for undisputed overdue charges after notice and a ten-day cure period. Annual adjustments include a fixed 3% license increase from 1 April 2028 and power rate changes only with 60 days' notice and documented energy cost changes. Service levels set 99.95% monthly power availability at the rack PDU, Severity 1 (loss of both feeds, 15-minute acknowledgement) and Severity 2 (single-feed degradation, 60-minute acknowledgement), and credits of 2% of the monthly license charge per full 30 minutes of unavailability, capped at 20%, claimable within 20 days. Physical security requires continuous CCTV with 90-day retention, badge logs, a staffed desk, up to eight authorized technicians for Suite D-14, 24-hour visitor registration with escort, and notice within four hours of confirmed unauthorized access. Maintenance occurs Sundays 02:00-06:00 Mountain Time with seven days' notice, plus emergency exceptions; remote hands include eight free hours monthly, then USD 110/hour, and customer change requests need 48-hour method statements, subject to provider rejection for risks. Data terms confirm customer ownership and control of applications and data, no provider inspection rights, and no provider-managed application backup.

structure.title: Page 007 - Maintenance, Change Windows and Remote Hands
structure.summary: The text covers colocation service terms: invoicing monthly on the first business day, net 30 payment, and a refundable USD 37,200 security deposit usable for undisputed overdue charges after notice and a ten-day cure period. It sets a 3% fixed annual license increase from April 2028 and allows power rate changes only with 60 days' notice and documented energy cost changes. Service levels include 99.95% monthly power availability at the rack PDU, Severity 1 (loss of both feeds, 15-minute acknowledgement) and Severity 2 (single-feed degradation, 60-minute acknowledgement), and outage credits of 2% of the monthly license charge per full 30 minutes beyond allowed downtime, capped at 20%, with claims due within 20 days. Security provisions require continuous CCTV and badge logs, 90-day recording retention, up to eight authorized technicians for Suite D-14, 24-hour visitor registration with escort, and notice within four hours of confirmed unauthorized physical access. Maintenance occurs Sundays 02:00-06:00 Mountain Time with seven days' notice, with emergency exceptions. Remote hands include eight hours monthly, with extra time at USD 110/hour in 15-minute increments and a one-hour minimum. Customers must submit method statements 48 hours before material changes, and Provider may reject changes threatening cooling, fire protection, or neighbors. Customer retains ownership and control of its data, Provider has no inspection rights, and Provider does not provide application backup.

structure.title: Page 008 - Data Responsibility and Confidentiality
structure.summary: The text covers a colocation/power services agreement across several sections: payment terms (monthly invoices net 30, USD 37,200 refundable security deposit usable after notice and cure, 3% annual license increase from April 2028, power rate changes need 60 days notice); availability commitment of 99.95% monthly power with severity levels, acknowledgement times, and outage credits (2% per 30 minutes, capped at 20%, claims within 20 days); physical security (CCTV retention 90 days, badge logs, up to eight authorized technicians, 24-hour visitor registration, four-hour breach notice); maintenance windows (Sunday 02:00-06:00 MT, seven days notice, emergency exceptions); remote hands (eight free hours monthly, USD 110/hour overage); change control (48-hour method statement, provider rejection rights); data ownership and confidentiality (three-year survival, compelled disclosure rules); liability cap (twelve months' charges), insurance requirements, and termination for cause (30-day or 15-day cure); equipment removal within 20 Business Days; formal notice methods; and Colorado governing law with Denver venue.

structure.title: Page 009 - Liability, Insurance and Termination
structure.summary: The text covers confidentiality obligations: parties use each other's Confidential Information only to perform the agreement with reasonable care, with ordinary obligations surviving three years and trade secrets protected while they qualify under law. Compelled disclosures are allowed only as legally required with advance notice where permitted, and access credentials cannot go to subcontractors lacking a need to know. Liability is capped at twelve months of recurring license charges, excluding fraud, willful misconduct, unpaid fees, and confidentiality breaches. Insurance requires Provider to carry USD 2 million general liability and USD 5 million cyber coverage, while Customer insures its own equipment. Termination for cause requires a 30-day cure period for material breach, or 15 days for nonpayment of undisputed invoices after default notice. Equipment removal must occur within 20 Business Days after service ends, with supervised access and possible storage fees. Formal notices require overnight courier or registered mail with email copy; email and tickets alone are invalid for termination. Colorado law governs, with exclusive venue in Denver courts, and urgent injunctive relief is permitted.

structure.title: Page 010 - Exit, Notices and Governing Law
structure.summary: The text covers confidentiality obligations: each Party may use the other's Confidential Information only to perform the agreement, with reasonable care; ordinary obligations survive three years post-expiration, while trade secrets remain protected as long as they qualify under law. Compelled disclosures are allowed only as legally required, with advance notice where permitted, and access credentials cannot be shared with subcontractors lacking a documented need to know. Liability is capped at twelve months of recurring license charges, excluding fraud, willful misconduct, unpaid fees, and confidentiality breaches. Insurance requirements include Provider's USD 2 million general liability and USD 5 million cyber liability coverage, while Customer insures its own equipment. Termination for cause requires a 30-day cure period for material breach, or 15 days for nonpayment of undisputed invoices after default notice. Equipment removal must occur within 20 Business Days after service ends, with Provider offering supervised access and possibly charging storage fees.
